issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court has power to transfer a suit pending on the original side of one High Court to another High Court in a different State.
material_facts: The suit was pending on the original side of a High Court in one State.
The petition sought transfer of the suit to a High Court in another State.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court had jurisdiction to entertain the transfer petition and transfer the suit between the High Courts.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, confers on the Supreme Court a new and broadly stated power to transfer cases between courts in different States when expedient for the ends of justice. High Courts stand on the same footing before the Supreme Court; the Court relied on Article 366(14) of the Constitution read with section 3(25) of the General Clauses Act. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

predicates.interstate_civil_transfer_application: A party applied to transfer a civil case from a court in one State to a court in another State.
predicates.case_pending_in_high_court: The case sought to be transferred was pending before a High Court.

issues.definition: When a civil transfer application concerns a case pending before a High Court in another State, the Supreme Court may transfer the case between High Courts.

issues.legal_issue: A prima facie case that a suit was deliberately instituted in a court lacking territorial jurisdiction may be considered as an additional factor in deciding a transfer application.
material_facts: The applicants contended that the pleadings showed the alleged publication occurred outside the jurisdiction of the court where the suit had been filed.
The court found a strong possibility that the territorial-jurisdiction objection could be accepted, while leaving the final jurisdiction question undecided.
issues.conclusion: A prima facie justified objection that a suit was instituted in the wrong court may be taken into account as an additional factor in deciding whether to transfer it; the Court did not finally determine territorial jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: In deciding an application under section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a court may consider a prima facie, pleadings-based claim that the suit was deliberately brought in the wrong court as an additional factor. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

predicates.civil_transfer_application: A party applied to transfer a civil suit from the court where it was filed.
predicates.pleadings_support_wrong_forum_objection: The pleadings provided prima facie support for the contention that the suit had been filed in a court without territorial jurisdiction.

issues.definition: In a civil transfer application, a pleadings-supported objection that the suit was filed in the wrong forum may be considered as an additional transfer factor.

issues.legal_issue: Whether transfer is expedient for the ends of justice depends on the totality of the circumstances, including the parties’ relative hardship and the practical convenience of trial.
material_facts: The defendants lived and carried on business in the proposed transferee city, and defending the suit in the original city would cause them great hardship.
The plaintiff had family in the proposed transferee city and had earlier brought related proceedings there.
The damages suit arose from pleadings in those earlier proceedings, making records and witnesses more convenient to produce in the proposed transferee city.
The Court considered the parties’ relationship, the nature of the suit, and the circumstances in which it had been filed.
issues.conclusion: Transfer of the suit to the proposed transferee High Court was expedient for the ends of justice, and the transfer petition was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires expediency for the ends of justice to be assessed on the totality of the facts and circumstances. Relevant considerations include hardship to the parties and the convenience of a smooth and speedy trial, including access to records and witnesses. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

predicates.interstate_civil_transfer_application: A party applied to transfer a civil case from a court in one State to a court in another State.
predicates.substantial_defence_hardship: Defending the suit in the original forum would cause a party substantial hardship.
predicates.trial_convenience_favors_transferee: The proposed transferee forum would make trial more convenient, including the production of records or witnesses.

issues.definition: For an interstate civil transfer application, substantial defence hardship or greater trial convenience in the proposed transferee forum supports a finding that transfer is expedient for the ends of justice.

issues.legal_issue: The possibility that transfer may deprive a plaintiff of procedures available in the original court does not by itself prevent the Supreme Court from entertaining a transfer application.
material_facts: The plaintiff argued that transfer would deprive him of procedures available in the original High Court.
The Court found no impediment to entertaining the transfer petition on that basis, while leaving questions about the application of the relevant provision to the transferee High Court.
issues.conclusion: The asserted loss of procedures available in the original court did not prevent the Supreme Court from entertaining the transfer petition; the Court expressed no opinion on how the transferee court should deal with any related procedural question.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the asserted procedural disadvantage did not create an impediment to entertaining the petition under section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It left the application of section 25(5) to any later question before the transferee High Court. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

predicates.civil_transfer_application: A party applied to transfer a civil case to a court in another State.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_loss_of_original_forum_: The plaintiff contended that transfer would deprive the plaintiff of procedures available in the original forum.

issues.definition: In a civil transfer application, a plaintiff’s claim that transfer would remove access to original-forum procedures does not bar the application from being entertained.
